Stake A · 0 ft · How it goes up

Nothing gets dug until the string is right

Post 07 · 48 ft

  1. 01 · 0 ft

    Stake the corners

    We walk the lot with your plat map, find the corner pins and pull a string between stakes. The string is the fence before there is a fence.

  2. 02 · 8 ft

    Call 811

    We call 811 and wait for the paint and flags. If a gas line runs where the gate post goes, the post moves.

  3. 03 · 16 ft

    Dig below the frost line

    Every hole goes below the frost line, so a cold Boise winter can’t heave a post out of the ground.

  4. 04 · 24 ft

    Set posts in concrete

    Posts every 8 feet, plumb to the string, set in concrete. It’s written on your quote.

  5. 05 · 32 ft

    Hang the rails

    Top, middle and bottom rails, level to the string, so the boards have something straight to hang on.

  6. 06 · 40 ft

    Put the pickets on

    Cedar or vinyl, even gaps, tops cut to one line from stake to stake.

  7. 07 · 48 ft

    Hang the gate, walk the line

    Steel frame inside, self-closing hinges. Then we walk the fence with you before we pack up.

Post 09 · 64 ft · Under the grade

The part you never see holds up the part you do.

A fence leans because of its posts. Ours go in the same way on every job, and it is written on the quote.

Every 8 ft
Posts on 8-foot centers, never stretched to save one.
In concrete
Each post sits in a concrete footing, crowned at the top so water runs away from the wood.
Below frost
Deep enough that frozen ground can’t lift it in a hard winter.
Plumb to the string
Checked with a level against the string before the concrete sets.

Sample post promise If a post we set leans in the first 5 years, we come back and reset it at no charge.

Post 13 · 96 ft · Questions

Questions we hear at the fence line.

Not on the list? Call (208) 555-0134. Dale H. answers most of them himself.

Who finds the property line?

We walk the lot with your plat map and find the corner pins before anything is staked. If a pin is missing, a surveyor sets it first. We don’t guess at a line.

Do I need a permit or HOA sign-off?

Often, yes, for taller fences, pool barriers and raised decks. We check what your city and your HOA ask for before we order material, and we build to those rules.

What about buried gas and power lines?

We call 811 before anyone digs and wait for the paint and flags. Posts move around lines, never the other way.

Wood or vinyl?

Cedar looks warm and takes stain, and it goes grey in the sun without it. Vinyl needs no stain, only a hose. Both get the same posts and the same string.

How do your decks hold up?

We frame at 12 inches on center and tape and flash the ledger where the deck meets the house. We show you the flashing before it’s covered.
